To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the empirical mean of any bounded and measurable function of the inputs to a learning algorithm converges to the expected value of that function, and that this convergence can occur even when the inputs are generated from a stationary, alpha-mixing process with an alpha-mix- ing coefficient that converges to zero arbitrarily slowly.

1) the empirical mean of any bounded function of a stationary alpha-mixing process converges to its expectation at a rate that depends only on the alpha-mixings of the process, and not on its geometric decay rate; and 2) PAC learning of any class of functions is possible if the alpha-mix of the data-generating distribution converges at a rate that is slower than the inverse of a polynomial of degree 1.5.
